newsitem.title: ISRAEL: U.S. Mideast envoy postpones departure.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Mideast envoy postpones departure.

text.p: U.S. Middle East envoy Dennis Ross, brokering an elusive Israel-PLO deal on the West Bank town of Hebron, has cancelled plans to leave for home on Sunday, a U.S. official said.

"Ross is not leaving tonight," the official, who asked not to be identified, told Reuters after Jordan's King Hussein wrapped up talks with Palestinian President Yasser Arafat in Gaza and prepared to travel to Tel Aviv to meet Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.
"There could be a meeting between Mr Netanyahu and Mr Arafat tomorrow (Monday)," the official said.
Arafat's spokesman Nabil Abu Rdainah said King Hussein and Arafat had telephoned Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak "and discussed with him a new formula that will be presented to Netanyahu tonight".
Abu Rdainah gave no details about the proposal.
The U.S.-brokered talks on a long-overdue Israeli troop redeployment from Hebron are at an impasse over the timing of three further withdrawals from largely rural areas of the West Bank.
